DONATO Cha • erson IP C ngress IPD Office, Capitol Compound Alab l, Sarangani Province Dear Mr. Donato: DILG Legal Opinion No. 07, S. 2013 22 FEB pn13 This has reference to your letter dated 22 January 2013 inquiring from the Depa ment about the legal process for payment of compensation and other emoluments of Indi nous Peoples Mandatory Representatives (IPMRs) to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and ther local sanggunians in the Province of Sarangani. Specifically, you posed the follo •ng queries: • Is there a need to create a position or plantilla for an IP representative prior to allocation of fund? • What if the concerned committee of the Sanggunian does not pass a resolution providing appropriation for IP representative? Are there any sanctions imposable against any of' these officials? IVhat is the role of DILG office against those localities vehemently refuse to recognize/accept the chosen IP representatives? What are the appropriate remedies if the sangguniangpanlalawigan or the local chief executive does not include the budget of IPMR in the ensuing fiscal year? • What are the processes of appropriating finds for IP representative?" As you narrated in your letter, there appears to be a conflict between the legal opini ns respectively rendered by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM)- Regi nal Office, Koronadal City and this Department in its DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, serie of 2011: Opinion ofDBM-Regionai Office: "xxx said position (Indigenous Peoples Mandatory Repr sentatives) shall be created which shall be adequately provided with funding requi ements for basic salary, including the associated compensation attached to the posit' n." DILG Legal Opinion No. 20, series of 2011: "(M)ay we emphasize that the concerned local anggunian has to enact an ordinance providing for the appropriation of funds for the salari and other emoluments to be given to the concerned ICC/IP representative." Hence, your subject letter to this Department. 20 a'

As to your first query, we are of the view that there is no longer need on the part of local government units (LGUs) to create a position or plantilla of Indigenous People Man atory Representatives (IPMRs) since Section 161 of Republic Act No. 83712 has by itself creat d a seat for Indigenous Peoples/lndigenous Cultural Communities (IPs/ICCs) repr entative when it mandated the mandatory representation of IPs/ICCs in policy-making bodi s and other local legislative councils. This was reiterated under Section 6, Part I, Rule IV3 0 the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) Administrative Order No. I, serie of 19984 and Section 8, Title 115 of NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 20096. In view of such creation of the position of IP MR under Republic Act No. 8371, the IPM shall have the same compensation, benefits and other emoluments as the regular mem ers of the concerned legislative bodies as prescribed under Republic Act No. 71607. With regard to your second query, the concerned Sanggunians needs to enact the Ann al Appropriations appropriating therein funds covering the salaries and appropriate bene Its and/or emoluments of the IPMR, not a mere resolution. This is pursuant to the Sec on 16. Right to Participate in Decision -Making. - ICCs/IPs have the right to participate fully, if they so choos , at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through proce ures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Conse uently, the State shall ensure that the ICCs/IPs shall be given mandatory representation in policy- male g bodies and other local legislative councils. 0th rwise known as the "Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997". Sec on 6. Mandatory Representation in Policy Making Bodies. The ICCs/IPs shall be provided mandatory repre ntation in all policy making bodies and in local legislative councils. ICC/IP representation shall be propo 'Onate to their population, and shall have the same privileges as the regular members of the legislative bodie and/or policy making bodies. ICC/I representatives shall be qualified and chosen by their own communities in accordance with a process to be de ermined by them. In consultation with ICCs/IPs, the NCIP in close coordination with DILG shall come •th appropriate measures to ensure the full participation of ICCs/IPs in matters affecting their up devel pment. Such measures shall also include the provision of technical assistance to develop the ICC/ IP repre ntative's knowledge of traditional socio-political systems, customary laws, justice system and skills in interf cing with non-lP governance and policy making. Rul s and Regulations Implementing Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as "The Indigenous Peoples' Right Actof 1997." Sec on 8. Powers, Duties, Functions. The powers, duties and functions of IP mandatory representatives shall be th same as that of the regular members of local legislative councils as provided in the Local Government Code of 1991, otherwise known as IRA 7160, and other applicable laws. However, IPs mandatory repre ntatives shall focus on the representation of the collective interests of ICCs/IPs•, ensure support for the sustai ed constitution and operations of the IPCB in their respective areas of jurisdiction; and maintain the devel pment and practice of ICCs/IPs traditional leadership titles and structures, justice systems, conflict resol •on institutions, and peace building mechanisms and processes that are compatible with the national legal stem and with internationally recognized human rights. Nati nal Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Councils Sect. 6, Part 1, Rule TV, NCIP AO No. 1, series of 1998; Section 13, NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009.

As already discussed above, since the position Of IPMR was created and mandated unde Republic Act No. 8371, we find the corresponding appropriation of their salaries and appr priate benefits and/or emoluments in the LGU's Appropriation Ordinance also man tory. The unjustified failure or refusal by the Local Chief Executive (LCE) and/or sang nian to include an item in the Appropriations Ordinance covering the salaries and appr priate benefits and/or emoluments of the IP MR is compellable by mandamus pursuant to Se tion 310, Rule 65 of the Revised Rules of Court. Administrative charges may also be filed gainst the concerned local elective officials pursuant to Section 6011 of Republic Act No. 7 60 or Section 1912 of Republic Act No. 677013. Sect on 3, Rule 65, Revised Rules of Court- Petition for mandamus.—When any tribunal, corporation, board, office or person unlawfully neglects the performance of an act which the law specifically enjoins as a duty resulti g from an office, trust, or station, or unlawfully excludes another from the use and enjoyment of a right or off e to which such other is entitled, and there is no other plain, speedy and adequate remedy in the ordin course of law, the person aggrieved thereby may file a verified petition in the proper court, alleging the fa ts with certainty and praying that judgment be rendered commanding the respondent, immediately or at some ther time to be specified by the court, to do the act required to be done to protect the rights Of the petitio er, and to pay the damages sustained by the petitioner by reason of the wrongful acts of the respondent. e petition shall also contain a sworn certification of non-forum shopping as provided in the third paragr ph of section 3, Rule 46. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. - An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or remov d from office on any of the following grounds: (a) Disloyalty to the Republic of the Philippines; (b) Culpable violation of the Constitution; (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; (e) Abuse of authority; (f) Unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive working days, except in the case of members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, Sangguniang bayan, and sangguniang barangay;' (g) Application for, or acquisition of, foreign citizenship or residence or the status of an immigrant of another country; and (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An el rive local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. Sect on 19, RA 6770 -Administrative Complaints. — The Ombudsman shall act on all complaints relating, but not li ited to acts or omissions which: (1) Ar contrary to law or regulation; (2) Arf unreasonable, unfair, oppressive or discriminatory; (3) Ar inconsistent with the general course of an agency's functions, though in accordance with law; (4) Pr ceed from a mistake of law or an arbitrary ascertainment of facts; (5) Ar in the exercise of discretionary powers but for an improper purpose; or (6) Ar otherwise irregular, immoral or devoid of justification. 0th rwise known as the Ombudsman Act of 1989.

As regards your third query, please be informed that the Department, being the gene al supervisor of all LGUs and their officials, has consistently reminded the LGUs' com liance to Republic Act No. 8371, specifically on the mandatory representation of IPs/I Cs in policy-making bodies and other local legislative councils. In fact, the Depa ment, in partnership with the NCIP, issued Joint Circular No. 001, series of 201114 man ating the sanggunian concerned to appropriate funds covering the salaries and appr priate benefits and/or emoluments of the selected IP/ ICC representative, which shall be an a ount similar to that received by the regular members of the local sanggunians as presc ibed under existing laws and at the same time giving unto the concerned local chief exe tive the responsibility of ensuring that funds covering the salaries of the selected IP/I C are included in the executive budget which he shall submit to the sanggunian and in the ual Appropriations thereafter enacted by the sanggunian15. Per the data provided by the NCIP and reports previously submitted by our Regional Offic s, LGUs failed to recognize or accept the selected IP MR due to the following reasons: a. b. c. d. e. g. h. Political reasons; No funds are available to cover the salaries/compensations of the IPMR; Loose and unreliable "Rules of Procedure" embodying the tribal system in the selection of IP representative; Duly-appointed IPMRs themselves lack the competence required to fully ventilate their concerns and sentiments during sanggunian sessions; Some groups are claiming representation in local sanggunians but could not present a certification from the NCIP; IPs/ICCs are recognized by the LGU but no representation in local sanggunians, LDC or any LSB; During the selection process, there was no coordination between the IPs and the DILG Field Officers assigned in the Municipalities; and Some of the members of the local sanggunians are IPs themselves thereby making IP representation technically present therein Except to letter (a) above, it can be deduced that LGUs have the difficulty in impl menting the mandatory representation of IPs/ICCs in the local sanggunians for unde tandable reasons. For cases falling under letter (a), it is advisable for the aggrieved party to file a petition for mandamus and appropriate administrative case/s as discussed above. With regard to cases falling under letter (b), LGUs relayed to us that they have diffi Ity in appropriating funds for the IPMR since in doing so they will exceed the Personal Serv' es limitation cap provided under Section 325 (a)16 of Republic Act No. 7160. Abad for possible issua ce of a Local Budget Circular delineating other ways on how LGUs could source out fund for the IPMR's salaries and appropriate benefits and/or emoluments without exceeding the P limitation cap provided under Republic Act No. 7160. As to cases falling under letters (c) up to (h), the Department is currently coordinating with the NCIP to remedy these issues. In fact, the NCIP, in coordination with the Depa ment, organized just recently a capacity-building seminar/workshop participated by IPM s from all over the country. We find that there is no longer need to answer your fourth and fifth queries since they ere already answered above. We hope that we have addressed your concerns accordingly. Very truly yours, ESUSB.
